subject: computation time for different methods of fscores

messages.author: 7b1c6e12e3ffdf0f
messages.subject: computation time for different methods of fscores
parts:
Hi Phil,
Is there a reason why the computation time for WLE is substantially greater than other methods -- even with mirtCluster? It is understandable that WLE will take longer than Bayesian methods because for example EAP is relatively computationally simple than WLE. But it takes up to 5X longer even when compared to ML.
Cheers,
Alvin


library(mirt)
library(irtoys)
dataNRM <- as.data.frame(irtoys::Unscored)
mirtCluster()

NRMmod <- mirt(dataNRM, 1,
                  itemtype='nominal')

timeEAP <- system.time(fscores(NRMmod, method="EAP", full.scores = TRUE))
timeWLE <- system.time(fscores(NRMmod, method="WLE", full.scores = TRUE))
timeML <- system.time(fscores(NRMmod, method="ML", full.scores = TRUE))
timeMAP <- system.time(fscores(NRMmod, method="MAP", full.scores = TRUE))
print(c(timeEAP[3], timeWLE[3], timeML[3], timeMAP[3]))

mirtCluster(remove=TRUE)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: computation time for different methods of fscores
parts: Hi Alvin,

On Thu, Jan 26, 2017 at 12:24 AM, Alvin <alv...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,
Is there a reason why the computation time for WLE is substantially greater than other methods -- even with mirtCluster? It is understandable that WLE will take longer than Bayesian methods because for example EAP is relatively computationally simple than WLE. But it takes up to 5X longer even when compared to ML.

In addition to computing the likelihood at each iteration of the optimisation of theta, which is very easy, the Fisher information function for each item must also be computed at the same time, which grows as the number of items increases. As none of mirt's Fisher information functions are optimised with C++ code, and all of them are wrapped within slower S4 dispatch methods, there comes to be a lot of overhead. I can try and fix a bit of the S4 overhead, but rewriting all the Fisher information functions to C++ isn't really something I'm interested in doing any time soon (the payoff is really only seen in computing WLEs, everywhere else their requirement is basically trivial). 

Phil

Cheers,
Alvin

messages.subject: Re: computation time for different methods of fscores
parts:
On Thu, Jan 26, 2017 at 11:03 AM, Alvin <alv...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks Phil!
As an aside, would you think that the bias-reduction advantage of WLE over ML compensates for the computation time required? In very large datasets and multiple runs, the time difference can be substantial.

It can be, but to me this is generally a non-issue. The bias becomes reduced as the test length increases, so using WLE is not typically required here, and in smaller tests WLE still shouldn't take too long to obtain. So the trade-off doesn't seem all that bad.
